summary: The note previews the first-ever "Maplewood Moves!" Fun Run and Walkathon on September 15, 2023, a community event meant to build unity, promote health, and raise money for after-school programs. It traces fun runs back to the 1960s and walking clubs of the 19th century, and covers the 5K route, organizers, sponsors, safety, youth involvement, and social media buzz. Quotes from organizers, a doctor, a sponsor, a student volunteer, and a first-time runner illustrate the event's goals.
one_line: Maplewood's first "Maplewood Moves!" Fun Run and Walkathon on September 15, 2023 aims to unite neighbors, promote health, and fund after-school programs.
key_facts: The first-ever "Maplewood Moves!" Fun Run and Walkathon is scheduled for September 15, 2023, in the Maplewood neighborhood.
Fun runs began in the 1960s as a quirky, low-pressure alternative to competitive marathons.
Sandra Thompson, a local schoolteacher, is the brains behind the event; a portion of registration fees will go to the Maplewood Community Center to fund after-school programs for kids.
The event has been in planning since early April by a coalition of local leaders including Sandra Thompson.
Jane Addams Park will be the starting point for the 5K course through tree-lined streets.
Tom Rodriguez, an organizing committee member, said the route is accessible for strollers and wheelchairs.
Dr. Maria Chen, a local general practitioner, says fun runs make exercise approachable; the event offers free workshops on stretching and nutrition before race day.
Raj Patel of Patel's Organic Groceries is a local business owner and sponsor of the event.
Officer Megan O'Reilly of the Maplewood Police Department will be on duty to ensure routes are traffic-controlled and monitored.
The event includes a "Retro Run" division where participants wear attire from decades past, and the latest timing technology will give runners performance data.
Local high school track and field teams will volunteer, and a mini fun run for children will precede the main event.
Luisa Gomez, a high school senior and track team captain, will mentor little kids at the event.
Hashtags #MaplewoodMoves and #CommunityOnTheRun are trending in local social media circles.
Michael Harris, a Maplewood resident and first-time runner, is participating as a milestone in his weight loss journey.
